---
title: Write a script with TypeScript
sidebar_label: Write a TypeScript script
description: Write a TypeScript script that saves a CSV report of a directory's files to your instance and lists the latest ones, with a key that reaches files and nothing else.
job: A builder writes a TypeScript script with a narrow key that saves and lists report files, and sees what the key can't do.
kind: tutorial
---

A script doesn't sign in as you. It carries a **key**, a secret that names exactly which types it may read or write, and works from any computer that reaches your instance.

- **You'll build** Reports, a TypeScript script that saves a CSV report of the files in a directory as a file on your instance and lists your last five reports.
- **You need** your own Marfa instance with the CLI signed in, as the [Quickstart](/quickstart) leaves you, at `http://localhost:8600`, and Node.js 22.18 or later.
- **You'll have** a script that runs on a key which can read and write files and nothing else.

<Steps paged>
<Step>

### Make a key for the script

Make a key that writes files:

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa keys create --label "Report script" --source reports --type-permission core.file=write
```

```text
marfa: writing to http://localhost:8600
marfa_k1_…
key 01a1fc70-1dfa-7783-9116-682a03979985 (Report script); the plaintext is shown once, keep it now
  core.file  Read and edit
```

</Terminal>

**Copy the line that starts `marfa_k1_` now:** Marfa shows the key once and keeps only a hash of it. `core.file=write` lets it read and write the type `core.file`, which holds ordinary files, and nothing else. `--source reports` labels every item the key creates, so an app can filter by it.

</Step>
<Step>

### Create the project

Install the [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) and TypeScript:

```bash
mkdir reports && cd reports
npm init -y
npm pkg set type=module
npm install @withmarfa/client
npm install --save-dev typescript @types/node
```

Node.js runs a `.ts` file by removing its types, so there is no build step, and TypeScript only checks them. Give it a `tsconfig.json`:

```json title="tsconfig.json"
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "module": "nodenext",
    "target": "esnext",
    "types": ["node"],
    "strict": true,
    "noEmit": true,
    "erasableSyntaxOnly": true,
    "verbatimModuleSyntax": true
  }
}
```

Tell the script where your instance is and which key to send, in the same terminal:

```bash
export MARFA_API_URL=http://localhost:8600
export MARFA_API_KEY=marfa_k1_…
```

</Step>
<Step>

### Save a report

Saving a file takes two requests: [upload its bytes](/reference/api/blobs/uploadBlob), then [create an item](/reference/api/items/createItem) that names them. Create `report.ts` with a client for your instance:

```ts title="report.ts"
import { createClient } from "@withmarfa/client";
import { readdir, stat } from "node:fs/promises";

const { MARFA_API_URL, MARFA_API_KEY } = process.env;
if (!MARFA_API_URL || !MARFA_API_KEY) {
  throw new Error("Set MARFA_API_URL and MARFA_API_KEY first.");
}
const marfa = createClient({ baseUrl: MARFA_API_URL, credential: MARFA_API_KEY });
```

Add the report. It writes one CSV row for each file in the directory you run it from, and saves the result under a name that holds the time:

```ts title="report.ts"
const rows = ["name,bytes,modified"];
for (const name of await readdir(".")) {
  const info = await stat(name);
  if (info.isFile()) rows.push(`"${name.replaceAll('"', '""')}",${info.size},${info.mtime.toISOString()}`);
}
const stamp = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 19).replace(/[:T]/g, "-");

const upload = await marfa.POST("/blobs", {
  body: new TextEncoder().encode(rows.join("\n") + "\n"),
  headers: { "Content-Type": "text/csv" },
});
if (upload.error) throw new Error(`${upload.error.error.code}: ${upload.error.error.message}`);
const { data, error } = await marfa.POST("/items", {
  body: {
    type: "core.file",
    properties: { title: `report-${stamp}.csv`, blob_ref: upload.data.hash, mime_type: upload.data.mime_type },
    tags: ["report"],
  },
});
if (error) throw new Error(`${error.error.code}: ${error.error.message}`);
console.log(`Saved ${data.item.id}, version ${data.item.version}`);
```

Every call returns `data` when it works and `error` when Marfa refuses. **Check `error` first:** TypeScript then knows the shape of `data`. Branch on `error.error.code`, which stays the same, never on the message.

<Terminal>

```bash
node report.ts
```

```text
Saved 01a1fc70-4d6e-7b2f-a2d6-0d6b3c0e55a1, version 1
```

</Terminal>

The file is an **item**, with an ID and a version that rises each time it changes.

</Step>
<Step>

### List your reports

Add a read to the end of `report.ts`. It asks for the five newest files tagged `report`:

```ts title="report.ts"
const list = await marfa.GET("/items", {
  params: { query: { type: "core.file", tags: "report", limit: 5 } },
});
if (list.error) throw new Error(`${list.error.error.code}: ${list.error.error.message}`);
for (const file of list.data.data) {
  if ("id" in file) console.log(`${file.properties.title}, ${file.properties.size_bytes} bytes`);
}
```

The `"id" in file` check tells TypeScript each entry is an item: a list that asks for metadata answers each item with its metadata instead. Check the types, then run the script again:

<Terminal>

```bash
npx tsc
node report.ts
```

```text
Saved 01a1fc70-9b3a-7c0e-8f41-5a7e2d19c3b4, version 1
report-2026-11-21-04-50-12.csv, 250 bytes
report-2026-11-21-04-49-58.csv, 250 bytes
```

</Terminal>

`npx tsc` prints nothing when the types are right. Each run saves another report, and the newest comes first.

</Step>
<Step>

### See what the key can't do

In the `body` of the write, change `type: "core.file"` to `type: "core.task"`, and run it:

<Terminal>

```bash
node report.ts
```

```text
Error: type_not_permitted: No access to type "core.task"
```

</Terminal>

Marfa refuses with `403 type_not_permitted`. **A key reaches only what you gave it,** so a script that leaks its key exposes your files and nothing else. [Errors](/reference/errors) lists every code.

Change the type back. To let the script write tasks too, widen the key from the CLI, using the ID from step 1. The key you hold changes in place:

```bash
marfa keys update <key-id> --type-permission core.file=write --type-permission core.task=write
```

Run it again with only `core.file=write` to narrow it back. [Manage keys](/use/manage-keys) covers expiry and revoking a key.
